::: {.hero-panel}
This exercise examines the geography of recorded armed conflict across Myanmar from January 2021 to September 2025. I analyse township-level event counts and reported fatalities with local spatial association and emerging hot spot methods, then test how sensitive the main findings are to location precision and neighbour definitions.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Main result"}
The analysis retains **53,899 recorded violence events** across 330 townships and 57 months. Gi* identifies 38 event hot spots, and 27 remain hot under both the precision-only and alternative-neighbour checks. Event frequency and reported-fatality patterns differ, so neither measure should be used as a substitute for the other.
:::

## Brief at a glance

The [official exercise brief](https://isss626-ay2026-27aug.netlify.app/take-home_ex02) requires three connected parts:

1. Prepare an analysis-ready township dataset and a complete space-time cube from the supplied ACLED records and MIMU v9.4 boundaries.
2. Use local measures of spatial association to locate significant clusters and spatial outliers, then apply EHSA to assess how the patterns change over time.
3. Communicate the results through a reproducible technical report and an executive summary of no more than ten slides, excluding the cover and contents pages.

The bonus component must answer an additional geospatial question and add a substantive insight. An extra map or package by itself does not qualify.

## Study design

The unit of analysis is the township and the time unit is the calendar month. The analysis keeps battles, explosions or remote violence, and violence against civilians. Event frequency and reported fatalities are analysed separately.

The main workflow is:

1. validate event identifiers, dates, coordinates, location precision, and fatality values;
2. assign eligible events to the official township polygons;
3. create all 330 × 57 township-month combinations;
4. calculate Local Moran's I and Gi* for accumulated township totals;
5. calculate space-time Gi*, test each township series with Mann-Kendall, and derive EHSA histories; and
6. test the event hot spots using stricter coordinate precision and an alternative spatial-neighbour definition.

::: {.callout-warning title="How to read the maps"}
These results describe recorded historical burden, not current individual risk. A grey or cold township is not automatically safe, and the analysis cannot account fully for differences in reporting access, displacement, population exposure, or uncertainty in reported fatalities.
:::

## Added analysis

The value-added section tracks the event-weighted geographical centre using comparable January-to-September windows. It asks whether the overall spatial balance of recorded events shifted between 2021 and 2025. Whole monthly spatial fields are resampled to show sensitivity to the months observed.

This extension complements the hot spot maps, but it is not interpreted as a moving conflict front or a prediction of future incidents.

## Reproducibility

The public repository omits the licensed ACLED event-level CSV and the private excluded-record audit. The [project README](https://github.com/davincuaso/ISSS608-VAA/blob/master/Take-home_Ex/Take-home_Ex02/README.md) explains where to restore the authorised course file or how to set its local path. MIMU boundary provenance, aggregate outputs, input checksums, package versions, seeds, validation checks, and the complete analysis code are included.
